transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-11-15
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~62 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Reeves (Redwood AE), Maya Singh (Redwood SE), Carlos Alvarez (Redwood CSM), Lisa Park (Silverpointe), Tom Benton (Silverpointe CTO), Rita Gomez (Security), Evan Mills (DevOps), Nina Chow (Product)

Summary:
- Kickoff for Silverpointe Health onboarding to Redwood (hosted + potential private deployment).
- Covered high-level rollout plan, security requirements (SOC2, SSO), pilot success criteria, and next steps for technical deep dive and documentation exchange.

Topics:
- Pilot scope and timelines
- Security/compliance (SOC2, SSO/SAML, KMS)
- Deployment options: hosted vs dedicated vs private (VPC/on-prem)
- Integration plan and success metrics

Transcript:
[00:00] Jordan Reeves: Hey everyone thanks for joining, um we'll do a quick intros then go through the onboarding plan, I'm Jordan AE on the account.
[00:12] Lisa Park: Hi all, Lisa here — Head of Data, happy to be on.
[00:15] Tom Benton: Tom, CTO, I'll jump in for the architecture bits.
[00:20] Rita Gomez: Rita, security at Silverpointe. I'll be listening for SOC2, KMS, audit logs stuff.
[00:25] Jordan Reeves: Great — Carlos from our CS team and Maya our SE are here as well.
[00:30] Carlos Alvarez: yep hi everyone.
[00:34] Maya Singh: hey, thanks. we'll try to cover the technical checklist and next steps.
[00:42] Jordan Reeves: So proposed timeline: 2 week pilot to start, then a phased rollout — pilot scope is query routing and embedding-based search in staging, production by Q1 — but that's flexible depending on security review and pilot results.
[00:58] Lisa Park: sounds good, what's the expected latency and cost profile for the pilot? we have a lot of short queries from our app.
[01:05] Maya Singh: to give a quick sense — for hosted, median token latency we're seeing is around 80-120ms for small models, but your volume and sequence length will matter. We can provide a benchmark run; for cost we recommend disabling the long-context models for pilot unless needed.
[01:22] Tom Benton: For us latency is critical, but we also have strict budget limits — we might prefer dedicated or private if it gives more predictable pricing.
[01:30] Jordan Reeves: totally — typical tradeoff. dedicated gives you reserved throughput and predictable unit cost; private gets you control over network and KMS but more ops. We recommend starting hosted for speed of rollout then a canary to dedicated or private.
[01:48] Rita Gomez: on private deployments — can you confirm encryption at rest AND support for our HSM? we need keys in our control.
[01:55] Maya Singh: yes, Redwood Private supports customer KMS / HSM integrations; we integrate with common KMS and can support bring-your-own HSM patterns, but we'll capture exact requirements in the security questionnaire.
[02:10] Evan Mills: Are there specific network requirements for VPC peering? Our infra team wants to know about NAT, egress, firewall rules.
[02:18] Maya Singh: we'll share a VPC network checklist — typically you need outbound to certain Redwood control plane endpoints, and a tunnel for private control plane installs. We'll list ports and IPs.
[02:30] Nina Chow: Quick Q — how do you handle model rollouts and regressions? We need an easy rollback if quality drops.
[02:37] Carlos Alvarez: we have rollout features — canary, A/B, automatic fallback to a stable variant. Plus quality monitoring tied to your prompt sets, we can alert on regressions.
[02:47] Tom Benton: What about logs and audit trails? Our compliance team will need detailed access logs.
[02:52] Maya Singh: audit logs are available; for Private you can retain logs in your bucket for longer retention. Hosted has configurable retention too, and we can discuss an enterprise retention add-on.
[03:05] Rita Gomez: Do you have a SOC2 or ISO cert? and pen test reports?
[03:09] Carlos Alvarez: we do — I'll share the SOC2 report and a summarized pen test PDF after the call (link).
[03:15] Lisa Park: Great. Also we'll want SSO/SAML and RBAC for onboarding.
[03:20] Jordan Reeves: yep SSO, SCIM provisioning, and role-based access are supported. Carlos will share the SSO setup guide.
[03:26] Tom Benton: For the pilot, we'll need to know how long a KV cache persists in the hosted offering — our use case depends on prefix caching.
[03:34] Maya Singh: caching depends on model and runtime; we can send you the default TTLs and we can tune them for the pilot. Also, we can recommend quantized model variants for cost.
[03:48] Evan Mills: What's the integration surface — SDKs, REST, webhooks?
[03:52] Maya Singh: SDKs for Python/Node, REST API, and webhooks for async events. We'll share code snippets.
[03:59] Lisa Park: for the pilot success criteria, I'd propose: 1) average latency under 250ms for our common queries, 2) cost per 1k requests under $X (we'll provide target), 3) no P0 security findings from your docs.
[04:12] Jordan Reeves: sounds reasonable — we can align on exact numbers.
[04:16] Tom Benton: timeline — can we have a benchmark run next week? we'd like data to decide between hosted/dedicated.
[04:22] Maya Singh: yes, we'll run a benchmark against a snapshot of your workload; please share sample queries and expected concurrency.
[04:30] Lisa Park: who will own the pilot on Redwood side?
[04:33] Jordan Reeves: Carlos is the CS lead, Maya will run the technical bits, and I'll handle onboarding and contract questions.
[04:40] Carlos Alvarez: I'll coordinate kick-off, test data intake, and an initial health check at the end of week 1.
[04:48] Rita Gomez: about data residency — our records must stay in-region (EU) for certain data. Can Redwood support region restrictions?
[04:55] Maya Singh: yes, we can pin deployments to specific regions; for hosted we have EU regions and for Private you can deploy on-prem or in your VPC in the required region. We'll document options.
[05:05] Tom Benton: Any gotchas around model quantization or accuracy regressions when you use int8 or other compression?
[05:11] Maya Singh: quantization can change outputs slightly; Redwood Optimize gives guidance on which model+quant profile preserves quality for your workload. We'll run evals against your prompt set as part of pilot.
[05:23] Lisa Park: Good — please include model quality eval in the pilot scope.
[05:26] Jordan Reeves: noted.
[05:29] (brief cross talk)
[05:40] Maya Singh: I'll need a list of endpoints, sample traffic patterns, and any blocked IPs so we can design the benchmark.
[05:47] Evan Mills: I'll get that to you, likely via secure share.
[05:51] Jordan Reeves: ok next steps recap: Jordan send onboarding plan + pricing; Carlos share SOC2 and SSO guide; Maya schedule technical deep dive and benchmark; Silverpointe to confirm pilot success criteria.
[06:05] Lisa Park: quick question on pricing — is there a minimum for dedicated?
[06:09] Jordan Reeves: yes dedicated has a monthly commit, will include options in the plan.
[06:15] Tom Benton: Can you also share a diagram of the private architecture?
[06:18] Maya Singh: yes, we'll attach a VPC/network diagram and the control plane architecture.
[06:23] (background noise)
[06:30] Rita Gomez: Will there be an NDA or data processing addendum?
[06:33] Jordan Reeves: we have a DPA and standard NDA. I'll surface the legal pack to your counsel.
[06:40] Carlos Alvarez: I'll also include contact points for escalation and support SLAs for the pilot.
[06:45] Nina Chow: Thanks, this was helpful.
[06:48] Jordan Reeves: cool — any other concerns?
[06:52] Lisa Park: none right now.
[06:54] Jordan Reeves: great, we'll follow up with docs and schedule the SE deep dive. Thanks everyone.
